rationale: Tests classification of abortion types based on cervical os status — a core differentiating feature
Tests the critical management principle that septic abortion requires antibiotics BEFORE evacuation
Tests the widely used clinical definition of RPL (3 or more consecutive losses)
Tests management of the most treatable cause of RPL — antiphospholipid syndrome requiring aspirin + LMWH
Tests the preferred modern evacuation technique — MVA is preferred over sharp curettage for early pregnancy
Tests the critical safety principle of checking uterine position before any evacuation procedure
Tests the discriminating serum β-hCG threshold (discriminatory zone) for ectopic pregnancy diagnosis
Tests the absolute contraindication to methotrexate — haemodynamic instability requires surgery, not medical management
Tests the key distinction between complete and partial hydatidiform mole based on karyotype and gross pathology
Tests the critical post-molar surveillance rule — contraception required during the entire β-hCG follow-up period
Tests the PUQE score as the validated clinical tool to grade severity of nausea and vomiting of pregnancy
Tests the critical thiamine-before-dextrose rule to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy in hyperemesis
